data.name: Gemariah
data.gender_notes: Gemariah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Gemariah means 'Exalted by God'. This name is derived from the Hebrew words ‘gamar’ which means 'exalted' and ‘yah’ which is a short form of God’s name YHWH. This name was borne by several figures in the Old Testament, including a priest and a prophet. The name Gemariah carries the meaning “Exalted by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gemariah usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gemariah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gemariah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: גמariah
in_hebrew.long_meaning: גמariah הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא השלם' או 'תמים'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'גמר' שפירושו 'תמים' או 'שלם', ו'אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם גמariah מוזכר בתנ''ך בספר ירמיהו, פרק לג, פסוק 12, שם גמariah הוא בנו של חלדיה, הנביא.

in_greek.name: Γεμαριας
in_greek.long_meaning: Γεμαριας είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα גמariah. Το όνομα σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι τέλειος' ή 'τέλειος από τον Θεό'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Γεμαριας, αλλά το εβραϊκό πρωτότυπο упоминается στο βιβλίο του Ιερεμία.

in_latin.name: Gemariah
in_latin.long_meaning: Gemariah est nomen hebraicum quod significat 'Deus est perfectus' vel 'perfectus a Deo'. Nomen Gemariah in Scripturis Sacris invenitur in libro Ieremiae, capitulo 33, versu 12, ubi Gemariah filius Chaldiae prophetae nominatur.

in_english.name: Gemariah
in_english.long_meaning: Gemariah is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name גמariah, meaning 'God is perfect' or 'complete'. The name is composed of two elements: 'gamar', meaning 'to complete' or 'to make perfect', and 'El', meaning 'God'. Gemariah is mentioned in the Bible in Jeremiah 33:12 as the son of Hilkiah, the prophet. The name signifies spiritual perfection and wholeness in God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gemariah is a Biblical name that carries a rich cultural significance for Christians. In the Old Testament, Gemariah appears as the name of two different individuals. The first is a priest who is a descendant of Aaron and serves under King Jehoiada during the reigns of King Jehoiachin and Zedekiah of Judah. The second is a prophet who writes down the words of Jeremiah. By using this name, Christians are reminded of the importance and continuity of God’s service throughout history, and the vital roles that both priests and prophets played in fulfilling God’s will.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gemariah holds a deep spiritual significance for Christians as it is a reminder that exaltation and honor come from God alone. The word 'Gemariah' itself means 'exalted by God', and by bearing this name, individuals are called to live their lives in a manner that is pleasing to God and brings honor to His name. Additionally, the name encourages believers to aspire to be exalted in God's presence and to seek His favor and blessings in all things. Ultimately, the name Gemariah calls individuals to live their lives with a comprehensive understanding of the importance of both faith and action, as they strive to serve God and fulfill His will in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gemariah: God's great interpreter. A name signifying the divine illumination and understanding bestowed upon one, enabling them to decipher the profound mysteries of God's Word.

historical_references.context: Gemariah is a priest living in Anathoth during the time of King Zedekiah of Judah. He and his family are spared from exile when they refuse to drink wine during a feast in honor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
